heading: PLACEHOLDER TEXT — replace before release
paragraphs: These are not real terms of use. This is placeholder content holding the space for wording supplied by a human. Do not rely on it, do not link to it and do not ship the app until reviewed legal text replaces it.
The blocks below exist only to show how the renderer sets a heading and the paragraphs beneath it.

heading: 1. Placeholder heading — scope of the service
paragraphs: This is where the description of what the app does, who it is for and what a user may expect from it will go. The paragraph is deliberately long so it is visible how a long run of text wraps at phone width and how the line height sits between the lines of one paragraph.
A second paragraph in the same block shows the gap between paragraphs.

heading: 2. Placeholder heading — user account
paragraphs: This is where the rules for creating, using and closing an account will go.

heading: 3. Placeholder heading — content added by the user
paragraphs: This is where it will be stated who owns the photos, service records and other data a user puts into the app.
And here, on what terms the app handles them.

heading: 4. Placeholder heading — liability and contact
paragraphs: This is where the limitation of liability and the operator's contact details will go.
